source: ar5iv LaTeXML HTML of arXiv papers first posted 2016 to 2021 with a published journal or conference version
purpose: Reference sections that are human-written, technical and peer reviewed. No chat model existed to write them. Models may have seen the papers in pretraining, so the corpus tests whether a rubric can tell human from model writing, not whether the model can recall the paper.

discovery.script: xar/discovery.py, run as `run.py discover-data`; output in data/discovery.json
discovery.openalex_filter: has an arXiv location, 100 to 1,500 citations, type article, not retracted, published 2016-01-01 to 2022-11-29
discovery.sample: seeded random sample of 10,000 matching works (seed 20261001)
discovery.arxiv_filter: first posted 2016 to 2021, last revised on or before 2022-11-29 (ChatGPT launched 2022-11-30), at most 20 authors, primary archive in one of the fields below
discovery.published_version: OpenAlex lists a journal or conference location marked publishedVersion
discovery.fields: cs and eess 9, math 8, stat/econ/q-fin 3, q-bio 5, astro-ph 6, cond-mat 7, hep/gr-qc/nucl 7, quant-ph 5, physics and nlin 6
discovery.order: Each field's eligible works are shuffled with a seed derived from the sample seed and the field name; the first 60 form its shortlist

eligibility: Walk each field's shortlist in order and keep the first papers up to the field's quota
ar5iv HTML with one abstract and unambiguous top-level introduction, with a related-work section and a conclusion section when the paper has them; at least 60 words per target section
At least 10 bibliography entries and no LaTeXML error markers or replacement characters
No title that suggests a survey, review, tutorial, overview, software, data release, catalogue, dataset or benchmark
No shared authors or title with a paper already selected; no paper about rubric optimization or this XAR procedure
Whole visible contexts and four-failure feedback fit every pinned endpoint without truncation
selection: Papers in field order, each field in shortlist order, are dealt to train 35, validation 16 and confirmation 5 in even steps along the list, so each split has papers from most fields; the pilot is the first 2 training papers
normalization: Whitespace normalization, equivalent HTML math/heading handling, one numeric citation style, text joined as written, and removal of figures, tables, listings and acknowledgements from the withheld reference; no expert rewriting
redistribution: Raw papers and extracted text stay local; publish identifiers, hashes and reconstruction commands. Licenses were not checked
inspection: Record agent extraction checks separately from human review; human suitability review remains an explicit acceptance gate
limitations: Highly cited papers may be memorized by the writer; the 30-word copy flag measures verbatim recall
Citation count and peer review are proxies for writing quality, not measures of it
ar5iv serves the latest arXiv version it converted, which can differ from the published text
Authors may have used editing services or non-native-speaker polishing before 2022; that is human work
Papers without a related-work section or a conclusion give fewer than 4 sections, so math papers contribute fewer examples
Papers whose introduction has no heading, such as Nature letters, and papers ar5iv could not convert are excluded
Selection favors papers whose LaTeX source converts cleanly, which skews against heavy custom macros
context_screen: Pinned official Qwen/Kimi tokenizers; maximum count with 25% headroom, four complete failure contexts and candidate pairs, 16000 feedback overhead tokens, and 16384 output tokens. Every actual request is checked again.
